title: Assistant Accountant
description:
Assistant Accountant

Stokenchurch Competitive salary, study support & good benefits Hybrid working

Are you a commercially minded, part-qualified accountant looking for a role where your analysis genuinely shapes business decisions?

We are seeking a proactive Assistant Accountant to join an established and growing commercial finance team in Stokenchurch. This is an excellent opportunity for an ambitious AAT, CIMA or ACCA studier to take ownership of meaningful commercial reporting, work closely with operational and client-facing colleagues, and develop within a collaborative, fast-paced environment.

You will sit at the centre of financial performance, helping to protect profitability, improve commercial visibility and turn financial data into clear, practical insight for stakeholders across the business.

The opportunity

Reporting to the Commercial Accounting Manager, you will support the delivery of accurate management information and robust financial control across revenue, cost of sales, gross profit and client or business-unit performance.

This is not a purely transactional accounting position. You will be encouraged to question, investigate, identify opportunities and communicate the story behind the numbers to non-financial stakeholders.

Key responsibilities
- Prepare and review monthly management accounts, including revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, accruals, prepayments and balance-sheet reconciliations.
- Analyse client, project, cost-centre and business-unit performance, identifying key variances, commercial risks and opportunities.
- Partner with internal teams and clients to prepare budgets, ensuring assumptions are robust and profitability is protected through appropriate inflationary and rate-card adjustments.
- Support forecasting and financial-planning activity with accurate data and commercially focused analysis.
- Produce clear, concise financial commentary for senior stakeholders to support informed decision-making.
- Maintain strong financial controls and ensure compliance with internal policies, accounting standards and audit requirements.
- Support month-end, year-end, statutory reporting and external audit processes.
- Identify and deliver improvements to reporting, processes, controls and the quality of commercial insight.
- Undertake ad-hoc analysis and finance projects in line with changing business priorities.

About you

You will be a confident and curious finance professional who enjoys understanding how a business operates-not simply reporting the results.

You will ideally bring:
- Part-qualified AAT, CIMA or ACCA status, with a commitment to completing your qualification.
- Previous experience within a commercial accounting, management accounting or finance business-partnering environment.
- Strong Excel capability and confidence handling, analysing and interpreting financial data.
- A sound understanding of revenue, costs, margins, budgets, forecasts and financial performance.
- The ability to communicate complex financial information clearly to colleagues outside finance.
- A proactive, improvement-focused mindset, with the confidence to challenge constructively and ask the right questions.
- An interest in keeping up to date with financial reporting requirements, regulatory developments and commercial finance best practice.
- Experience of PeopleSoft and/or Planning Analytics would be advantageous, but is not essential.

Why apply?

This role offers broad commercial exposure and the opportunity to make a visible contribution to the performance of the business. You will work closely with stakeholders across finance, operations and client teams, gaining the experience needed to progress your commercial finance career.

Alongside a competitive salary of 30-35k (depending on experience), you will receive a benefits package designed to support your professional development, financial wellbeing and work-life balance, including:
- A study support package for employees working towards their AAT, CIMA or ACCA qualification.
- Pension scheme.
- Life assurance cover.
- Income protection.
- 26 days' annual leave, plus bank holidays.
- Hybrid working - 3 days in the office.

If you are a capable part-qualified accountant seeking a role with genuine stakeholder engagement, ownership and development potential, we would welcome your application.

JOB DESCRIPTION

Position Title: Activity Coordinator

Reports To: Service Manager or Team Leader

Primary Objective: To design, coordinate and deliver a varied programme of engaging, accessible and employment-focused activities for young people aged 18 to 24. Internal

Service Manager and Team Leader

Mentors and Employer Engagement and Employer Services colleagues

Quality, Compliance, Performance, Safeguarding and MI teams

Wider Delivery Colleagues

External

Participants (young people aged 18 to 24) and, where appropriate and with consent, their support networks

Engagement Activity Partners, specialist subcontractors and community organisations

Jobcentre Plus, local authorities, education and training providers

Local employers, sector partners and venue providers

Key Responsibilities

Activity Design and Delivery

Design, coordinate and maintain a rolling programme of structured group and individual activities aligned with participants needs, aspirations, action plans and outcomes.

Deliver welcoming, energetic and inclusive sessions for young people aged 18 to 24, using age-appropriate interests such as sport, creative arts, technology, gaming, virtual reality, outdoor activities and community projects.

Prepare clear session plans, learning objectives, resources and contingency arrangements so every activity supports employability, personal development or progression.

Adapt pace, content and delivery for different communication styles, neurodiversity, disabilities, literacy levels, digital capability, confidence levels and reasonable-adjustment needs.

Participant Engagement and Development

Use trauma-informed, strengths-based and culturally responsive practice to build trust, promote participant choice and voice, and support those who lack confidence or have had negative experiences of services or education.

Help participants develop communication, teamwork, problem-solving, resilience, timekeeping, professional behaviours, digital skills and an understanding of workplace expectations.

Support young people to identify and present their transferable skills and achievements in CVs, applications, interviews and employer conversations.

Provide practical sector insight through employer talks, workplace visits, careers activities, mock recruitment exercises, volunteering and project-based learning.

Coordination and Partnership Working

Coordinate specialist partner delivery, including procurement or booking processes, schedules, venues, participant communications, accessibility, risk information, attendance, feedback and supporting evidence.

Work closely with Mentors to identify suitable activities, share relevant progress or concerns, and ensure learning is reflected in participant action plans and next steps.

Promote activities through engaging face-to-face and digital communications, use reminders and motivational contact, and promptly follow up non-attendance with the Mentor.

Build relationships with youth, community, education, health, specialist and employer partners to widen participation, strengthen referral routes and reduce barriers.

Contribute to programme events, outreach, sector pathways and employment-focused campaigns across sites and community venues.

Safeguarding, Inclusion and Professional Practice

Place participant welfare at the centre of delivery and follow safeguarding, lone-working, incident, whistleblowing and escalation procedures at all times.

Recognise and respond appropriately to safeguarding concerns, disclosures, exploitation risks or changes in presentation. Apply adult safeguarding procedures for participants aged 18 to 24 and follow child safeguarding processes where a concern also involves a child.

Maintain professional boundaries, confidentiality and appropriate use of digital communication and social media.

Obtain and record informed consent where required, share information only where there is an appropriate and lawful basis and comply with data protection requirements.

Quality, Compliance and Performance

Complete activity and venue risk assessments, dynamic risk checks, incident reports and emergency arrangements in line with organisational policy and health and safety requirements.

Maintain accurate, timely and audit-ready records of referrals, attendance, participation, adjustments, feedback, progress, outcomes, risk documentation and safeguarding actions.

Deliver the agreed activity schedule consistently, ensuring sessions start on time and resources, venues and partners are coordinated effectively.

Monitor attendance, engagement and completion, take timely action to address non-engagement, and evidence improvements in confidence, employability skills, workplace understanding and readiness for next steps.

Use participant and stakeholder feedback, attendance data and progression information to evaluate impact and continuously improve the activity offer.

Support progression to agreed next steps, including mentoring actions, training, employer engagement, interviews, work experience or employment.

Manage activity resources and agreed budgets responsibly, demonstrate value for money, and ensure equipment is safe, available and stored appropriately.

Professional Knowledge and Flexibility

Maintain current knowledge of youth employment challenges, local labour markets, digital trends and support available to 18 to 24-year-olds.

Work flexibly across locations and, where required, outside standard hours to meet participant and programme needs.

To deliver role responsibilities in line with organisational values and all relevant policies and procedures

Any other duties appropriate to the level of this role, for which the post-holder has the necessary training or experience.

Essential and Desirable Skills, Knowledge and Experience

Delivery and Engagement

Experience of planning, coordinating and delivering engaging group activities for young people or young adults, preferably including those aged 18 to 24 and those not in education, employment or training or facing multiple barriers.

Strong facilitation, presentation and engagement skills, with the ability to build rapport while maintaining clear boundaries and expectations.

Ability to turn creative or recreational activities into purposeful employability and personal-development learning and adapt delivery for different needs, abilities, cultures, communication styles and confidence levels.

Experience in employability, youth work, community development, education, careers, coaching or publicly funded services, including delivery of creative, digital, sports, gaming, virtual reality, outdoor, volunteering or project-based activities.

Participant Support and Safe Practice

Understanding of barriers affecting young people, including low confidence, poor mental wellbeing, disability, neurodiversity, caring responsibilities, housing instability, transport difficulties, digital exclusion and limited work experience.

Knowledge of adult and child safeguarding responsibilities, professional boundaries, equality,

Qualifications, Values and Flexibility

A relevant qualification in youth work, teaching, training, coaching, careers, employability, safeguarding, mental health first aid or facilitation.

A current first-aid qualification and experience of completing activity or venue risk assessments.

Commitment to participant voice, strengths-based practice, inclusion and high-quality customer service.

Ability and willingness to travel on a daily basis to different locations within assigned local area, to support participants, employers, events, placements and contract delivery (no homeworking is available due to the nature of the role)

Willingness to complete all required induction and refresher training, including safeguarding, equality, data protection and health and safety.
